subject: Literacy
title: Songs with actions
objectives: Children will sing and do actions to a song.
Children will remember words of a favourite song.
content: Body songs, animal songs and counting songs with actions, and remembering the words of a favourite song.
teachingActivities: Teach one song at a time with the same actions each day; sing slowly first and then at a normal speed; let children choose the next song; sing in a comfortable voice and never test children on words.
learnerActivities: Sing songs with actions, do the right action at the right word and remember a favourite song.
resources: A toy frog and a toy duck
assessment: Observe whether each child sings along with several songs and does the right action at the right word.
expectedOutcomes: Does the right action at the right word.

lessons.title: Head, shoulders, knees and toes
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will touch the right body part as they sing a body song.
successCriteria: Touches head, shoulders, knees and toes
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know rhymes from Term 1 and can hear rhyming pairs; many can sing along with actions.
lessons.starter: Touch your head and say "This is my head." Touch your knees and say "These are my knees." Ask "Where is your head?"
teacherActivities: Say each body part and touch it slowly: head, shoulders, knees, toes.
Sing the song slowly: "Head, shoulders, knees and toes, knees and toes" and do the actions.
Sing it a little faster and wait for the children to lead.
Let a child lead the song with the puppet.
learnerActivities: Children touch each part as you say it.
Children touch the parts and sing or hum.
Children do the actions at the right word.
Child leads and friends follow.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say each body part and touch it slowly: head, shoulders, knees, toes. Children: Children touch each part as you say it.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing the song slowly: "Head, shoulders, knees and toes, knees and toes" and do the actions. Children: Children touch the parts and sing or hum.
Step 3. Teacher: Sing it a little faster and wait for the children to lead. Children: Children do the actions at the right word.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child lead the song with the puppet. Children: Child leads and friends follow.

practical.title: Body song
steps: Stand in a circle with space.
Sing the song and touch each part.
practical.safety: Leave space around each child so no one bumps. Stop when children look tired and sit down to rest.

differentiation.support: Touch the child’s head, shoulders, knees and toes gently with the words.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to sing it quietly and then loudly.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Sing the song very slowly and sit down.
lessons.homeConnection: Sing the song at bath time and touch each body part.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "touch the right body part as they sing a body song" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Five little ducks
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will join in the actions and words of a counting song about ducks.
successCriteria: Holds up fingers or says a number
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know rhymes from Term 1 and can hear rhyming pairs; many can sing along with actions.
lessons.starter: Hold up the toy duck and say "Quack, quack." Ask "Can you quack?"
teacherActivities: Sing "Five little ducks went swimming one day. Over the hill and far away." Show five ducks on the cloth.
Sing again and take one duck away each time.
Sing again and wait for the children to say "quack".
Let each child move a duck across the blue cloth.
learnerActivities: Children watch the ducks and say "quack".
Children hold up fingers or point to the missing ducks.
Children say "quack, quack".
Child moves a duck and says quack.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing "Five little ducks went swimming one day. Over the hill and far away." Show five ducks on the cloth. Children: Children watch the ducks and say "quack".
Step 2. Teacher: Sing again and take one duck away each time. Children: Children hold up fingers or point to the missing ducks.
Step 3. Teacher: Sing again and wait for the children to say "quack". Children: Children say "quack, quack".
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child move a duck across the blue cloth. Children: Child moves a duck and says quack.

practical.title: Ducks on the water
steps: Spread a blue cloth on the floor.
Each child holds a paper duck.
Sing the song and move the ducks across the cloth.
practical.safety: Use paper or cloth ducks and keep the cloth flat to avoid tripping. Supervise movement.

differentiation.support: Hold up the child’s fingers as you sing the numbers.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count the ducks that are left.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many ducks are left?
questions.expected: The number left, by fingers or word.

expectedOutcomes: Says quack at the right time
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to the ducks as they swim away.
lessons.homeConnection: Sing "Five little ducks" at home and use fingers to count.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "join in the actions and words of a counting song about ducks" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Five little ducks went swimming one day. Over the hill and far away.

lessons.title: Frog on a log
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will do the actions of a song about a frog and a log.
successCriteria: Jumps like a frog on request
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know rhymes from Term 1 and can hear rhyming pairs; many can sing along with actions.
lessons.starter: Hop the toy frog along the mat and say "Ribbit, ribbit. Frog is hopping."
teacherActivities: Sing "Little frog, little frog, hop, hop, hop. Sit on the log and stop, stop, stop."
Sing again and let children hop on the spot.
Wait for children to say "hop" and "stop".
Let each child be the frog and sit on a log.
learnerActivities: Children listen and hop with their fingers.
Children hop on the spot on "hop" and sit on "stop".
Children say the words.
Child hops to the log and sits.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing "Little frog, little frog, hop, hop, hop. Sit on the log and stop, stop, stop." Children: Children listen and hop with their fingers.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing again and let children hop on the spot. Children: Children hop on the spot on "hop" and sit on "stop".
Step 3. Teacher: Wait for children to say "hop" and "stop". Children: Children say the words.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child be the frog and sit on a log. Children: Child hops to the log and sits.

practical.title: Hop to the log
steps: Place a soft log or cushion on the floor.
Children hop towards it and sit when the song says stop.
Repeat with each child as frog.
practical.safety: Keep the area clear and hop on a soft mat. Limit the hopping to short bursts to avoid tiredness.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and hop together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to hop three times and then sit.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Settle like a sleeping frog on the log.
lessons.homeConnection: Hop like a frog at home and sing the song with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "do the actions of a song about a frog and a log" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Little frog, little frog, hop, hop, hop. Sit on the log and stop, stop, stop.

lessons.title: Choose a song
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will choose and sing a favourite song with the group.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know rhymes from Term 1 and can hear rhyming pairs; many can sing along with actions.
resources: Picture cards for the body song, ducks and frog
lessons.starter: Show the three picture cards and say "Which song shall we sing?" Let a child pick one.
teacherActivities: Show the three cards and let a child pick one from the basket.
Sing the chosen song with the actions.
Pick another card and sing again.
Let each child hold the puppet as the singer.
learnerActivities: Child chooses and the group sings.
Children sing and do the actions.
Children join in.
Child sings with the puppet.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the three cards and let a child pick one from the basket. Children: Child chooses and the group sings.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing the chosen song with the actions. Children: Children sing and do the actions.
Step 3. Teacher: Pick another card and sing again. Children: Children join in.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child hold the puppet as the singer. Children: Child sings with the puppet.

practical.title: Song basket
steps: Put three song cards in a basket.
Each child picks one and the group sings it.
Repeat until every child has chosen.
practical.safety: Keep voices gentle and give water if needed. Supervise passing the basket.

differentiation.support: Sing softly in the child’s ear and do the actions together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to sing a verse alone or with a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Does the right action at the right word
lessons.conclusion: Sing the favourite song once more and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child choose a song at home and sing it with you.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "choose and sing a favourite song with the group" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 6 songs check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child sings and does actions.
successCriteria: Does the right action at the right word
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know rhymes from Term 1 and can hear rhyming pairs; many can sing along with actions.
lessons.starter: Sing the body song and show three song stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: body song, ducks and frog.
At each station sing a song and watch the child’s actions.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child sings and does actions.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: body song, ducks and frog. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station sing a song and watch the child’s actions. Children: Child sings and does actions.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Song stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep the floor clear. Use soft toys and paper props.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and sing the same song.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to lead a song.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: sings along; does the right action at the right word; remembers the words of a favourite song.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 6
lessons.conclusion: Sing a quiet goodbye song and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Sing three songs at home each day with actions.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child sings and does actions" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
